transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Rogers (Atlas - Platform Eng), Lina Martinez (Atlas - Head of ML), Marcus Chen (Atlas - SRE)

Summary:
Quick walkthrough of Redwood Console's tracing, error analysis, and request logs. Focus on debugging flows, correlating traces to request IDs, retention/retention policies, and security controls for Private/Dedicated. Customer asked about latency attribution, KV cache visibility, and how to debug failed generations and request timeouts. Agreed next steps: send security and compliance artifacts, run a POC benchmark with Atlas sample logs, and follow-up on Private deployment options.

Topics:
- Tracing (trace IDs, spans, root-cause analysis)
- Request logs (filters, exporting, redaction)
- Error analysis (common model errors, fallback policies)
- Debugging flows (how to reproduce, correlate events, live tail)
- Security / Private deployment questions (VPC, KMS, audit logs)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got, uh, about 45 minutes, we can run through the console and then open it up for Qs.
[00:12] Sam: yeah sounds good, uh, we're mostly curious about tracing and request logs — how we can triage production errors quickly, it's been a pain point.
[00:20] Priya: great, I'll share my screen and show the tracing view. quick note, some of the names in the UI might say "Redwood Console" or older labels, our export's fine but the live UI sometimes shortens service names.
[00:35] Lina: no problem, go ahead.
[00:40] Speaker 2 (screen share): ok so on the left nav you'll see Traces -> Request Traces. i'll filter to the last 24 hours, and we get a list of trace IDs with latencies. we surface the top latency span, status codes, and the model variant used.
[01:05] Marcus: can you tie that back to the actual request id from our app? we need to correlate with our logs.
[01:12] Priya: yes, we include a request_id field by default if you send x-request-id; otherwise the console shows the internal trace id which you can search for in request logs. i'll show a cross-link: click a trace, then "open request log" and it navigates to the request log entry with the same id.
[01:30] Jordan: (background) and that link maintains path for private customers with VPC access as well.
[01:37] [00:01:45] Sam: quick q, what about prefix/KV cache misses? can we see cache hit rates per route?
[01:46] Priya: yes, under the trace details we break down token-level timing and you can see a "kv cache" span. we also show aggregated cache hit/miss metrics per route on the model dashboard. sometimes the transcriber messes up, it's labeled k-v cache or kv-cache in older builds.
[02:10] Lina: is that down to the model or the runtime? like when we see a long tail, is it kernel selection or batching causing it?
[02:18] Priya: good question — we show the kernel path and hardware used in the trace metadata, e.g., cuda kernel 1 vs 2, quantized route. for batching we show wait time vs compute time. you can see if it's queuing (batching) or compute (kernel).
[02:40] [00:03:00] Marcus: about errors — we've seen occasional 5xx with "kv cache invalidation" and some timeouts, is there an automated alerting?
[03:07] Jordan: yes, you can set alert rules in Console; for POCs we often enable error rate + latency SLO alerts. we'll also surface automatic regression alerts if a rollout causes increased errors.
[03:22] Priya: i'll demo an error trace: click a failed trace, you see the stack of spans, the error message from the runtime, and a sample prompt + model response (if retention policy allows). note that in Private setup, you can configure redaction and not store raw prompts.
[03:45] Sam: that redaction option is important — we need to ensure PHI isn't stored. can you confirm how redaction works with audit logs?
[03:55] Priya: yes, for Private we integrate with customer KMS and you can enable on-the-fly redaction; audit logs still record metadata like trace id, timestamps, and which model version was used, but not PII. we'll send the SOC2/ISO docs that explain that in detail.
[04:12] Lina: and what about retention — can we set different retention for traces vs request bodies?
[04:18] Priya: yep, retention is configurable per-tenant and per-data type: traces, request logs, and full prompts. by default hosted keeps prompts for 30 days, traces for 90 — but for Private/Dedicated we can match your policy, including short retention for request bodies.
[04:35] [00:06:00] Sam: walk me through a real debugging flow — say a user hits a 504 from your API, what do we do?
[04:45] Priya: so step one, find the request id in your app logs. use our search to paste the id or the user id, filter timeframe. open the trace, look at the span waterfall — check for queuing (batch wait) and the compute span. if compute is small but overall latency is big, probably batching/queueing. if compute is large, we look at kernel and model variant. there's also "fallback" spans if a fallback model invoked.
[05:20] Jordan: and we added a feature to replay a request in a sandbox — you can re-run the exact request against the same model variant to reproduce. note: replay respects redaction and your data policies.
[05:38] Marcus: can we export a set of traces for a week to feed into our incident analysis tool?
[05:44] Priya: yes, exports are CSV/JSON, you can filter and then export. for larger exports we provide S3 delivery for Private or a signed link for hosted.
[06:00] Lina: how granular are the logs — do we have token-level timing?
[06:06] Priya: token level is available in traces — we show token buckets and aggregate 95/99 latencies. token-level payloads are optional because of size and PII concerns.
[06:20] [00:09:00] Sam: what's the overhead of tracing itself? does enabling full traces increase latency?
[06:27] Priya: negligible — traces are collected asynchronously; there's a small instrumentation overhead but not on the critical path. for ultra-low latency customers we can sample traces.
[06:40] Jordan: quick interruption — competitor mention: some folks try to do this with X infra or a self-hosted stack, but you're tradeoffing observability vs ops burden.
[06:52] Sam: yeah we looked at Anthropic and Replicate but their observability wasn't as integrated.
[06:58] [00:10:30] Priya: demoing Request Logs now. you can search by status code, latency range, model, route, and custom metadata tags (we encourage sending team and env tags). here i'll filter for 5xx in the last 6 hours.
[07:18] Speaker 1: ok there's a spike, here's a trace id, click it, you see the error message from the runtime, and a suggestion panel with likely causes — e.g., model oom, kv-cache miss, or transient infra error. the suggestions are heuristics.
[07:40] Lina: those heuristics are helpful. how do we tune them?
[07:45] Priya: suggestions are based on span patterns, but we can add custom heuristics for Dedicated customers during onboarding.
[07:55] [00:12:00] Sam: security again — for Private deployments does the console run in our VPC or via a control plane?
[08:02] Jordan: the control plane remains Redwood-run but the data plane can be in your VPC for Private, or on-prem package for air-gapped setups. access to logs and traces follows your network rules and KMS integration.
[08:16] Marcus: do we get full audit logs for who viewed traces and what they exported?
[08:21] Priya: yes, audit logs capture user actions — view, export, modify retention. they're integrated with our RBAC so you can restrict export privileges.
[08:34] [00:13:00] Sam: onboarding timeline — if we start a POC, how quickly can we have dedicated telemetry and SSO in place?
[08:40] Jordan: for a standard POC we can spin up a dedicated instance in 1-2 weeks; Private/VPC often takes 3-6 weeks depending on network review and KMS setup.
[08:52] Lina: cost question — if we enable verbose tracing, does that change billing substantially?
[08:58] Priya: traces themselves are lightweight; request-log retention and exports affect storage costs. we show cost estimates in the Optimize tab for different retention profiles.
[09:12] [00:15:00] Sam: ok can you show a live example of reproducing a failed request?
[09:18] Priya: sure — here's a failed trace, i click replay, it opens the sandbox, we run it and see the same error — in this case the runtime returned a truncated response due to a token limit mismatch. in the trace details you can see "truncate-span" and the exact tokenizer token count.
[09:40] Jordan: small aside — sometimes the transcript will say tokenizer vs tokeniser, sorry for the UK vs US.
[09:48] [00:16:30] Lina: if we pin a model version and then rollout a new quantized variant, can we do canary and have traces split by variant?
[09:57] Priya: yes, variant metadata is recorded; the Console supports canary rollouts and you'll see separate time series and trace distributions per variant so you can compare.
[10:12] Sam: can we set up automatic fallback to a smaller model on timeouts?
[10:18] Priya: yes, routing policies support fallback to compatible variants based on latency or errors; the trace will show both attempts and the final success/failure.
[10:30] [00:18:00] Marcus: question about observability retention — for compliance we might need 6 months of traces but only 7 days of request bodies. can you map that?
[10:38] Priya: absolutely — retention is policy driven. we can also pseudonymize or redact PII before storing.
[10:46] Sam: great. last bit — do you have examples of typical triage runbooks?
[10:52] Jordan: yes, we'll send a triage playbook. it covers steps: find request id -> open trace -> check queuing vs compute -> verify kernel/model variant -> check fallback behavior -> export traces for SRE.
[11:05] [00:19:30] Lina: that's helpful. can you also include details on how kernel selection appears in traces?
[11:10] Priya: yes, kernel selection is part of trace metadata — we log the compiled path and quantization profile.
[11:20] Sam: thanks.
[11:22] Jordan: ok quick recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO docs and the triage playbook, Priya will run a short request-log demo export and attach sample CSV, Sam will provide sample logs and a test key, Jordan will send Dedicated pricing and pilot agreement. Any objections?
[11:40] Sam: none, sounds good.
[11:42] Lina: nope, thanks everyone.
[11:44] Jordan: great, thanks all — we'll follow up via email and set up the POC kickoff.

Action items (as discussed in call):
- Priya to run sample request-log export and attach CSV (due 2027-09-21)
- Jordan to send security/compliance pack and Dedicated pricing (due 2027-09-16)
- Sam to share sample prod logs and temporary test key (due 2027-09-18)

End of transcript.
